house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.estimator: REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 1 degree(s) of freedom (t = 12.7062)
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.THE_POINT_ESTIMATE_IS_UNCHANGED: The published point is 0.9074 and the house-rule point is 0.9074. THE NUMBER A READER REMEMBERS DOES NOT MOVE; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives.

published_interval.restated_2026_08_20: The published interval is now REML, so this block compares a REML point interval against a REML Hartung-Knapp one and the ESTIMATOR is no longer one of the things that differ between them. At k=2 the moment estimator and REML coincide exactly, so not one digit of this block's numbers moved -- only the label, which was wrong.

house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.variance_inflation_floor: A FLOOR OF 1 IS APPLIED TO THE VARIANCE-INFLATION FACTOR so the adjustment can never NARROW an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a KNOWN problem with KNOWN handling rather than a novel judgement.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.no_rule_is_decided_here: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-20. The rule WAS decided, in DECISIONS-COCHRANE-2026-08-18.md section 1, and applied on 2026-08-20: REML is the estimator corpus-wide, and Hartung-Knapp is a SENSITIVITY analysis at k<=3 rather than the primary interval (Handbook 6.5 s10.10.4.4-10.10.4.5). Both intervals still stand on this page and nothing is unpublished.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.what_this_means_for_this_pool: THE PUBLISHED INTERVAL EXCLUDES 1 AND THE HOUSE-RULE INTERVAL CROSSES IT. A SIGNIFICANCE VERDICT TURNS ON THE INTERVAL METHOD ALONE. A reader shown only the published interval has been told something firmer than the evidence supports; a reader shown only the wider one loses that the contributing trials agree. BOTH ARE HERE.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.read_the_width_with_care: AT k=2 HARTUNG-KNAPP USES t ON ONE DEGREE OF FREEDOM -- 12.7062 against the normal 1.9600 -- and the interval is enormously wider. That width is a property of the method at very few studies, not a measurement of this evidence. It is recorded so a reader can see it; it is NOT presented as the better interval.

r_output.what_it_is: The fit that produces the numbers this block now publishes, printed by metafor and pasted unaltered. The previous fit, under the estimator this pool used before 2026-08-20, is kept beside it under r_output_superseded_2026_08_20 rather than discarded.
r_output.reproduction_of_the_previous_value: Before this refit was applied, the OLD estimator was refitted on the same inputs and checked against the stored value: REPRODUCED. A pool whose old fit did not reproduce was not overwritten.
r_output.why_this_was_re_run: THE PREVIOUS STORED OUTPUT QUOTED A FIT THAT DID NOT PRODUCE THIS PAGE'S NUMBERS. It printed 'tau^2 estimator: DL' where this object declares REML, at k = 2 -- and this project's own statistics rule forbids DerSimonian-Laird below k = 10. EVERY STORED NUMBER ON THIS OBJECT IS REML: the stored tau-squared and I-squared match a REML refit exactly. So the quotation was of a DIFFERENT FIT from the one behind the published values, presented verbatim as this engine's word. P56. Re-run under the declared estimator; NO PUBLISHED NUMBER MOVED -- the point, the interval and the heterogeneity all reproduce.

primary.estimator_note_2026_08_20: REML, applied 2026-08-20 under DECISIONS-COCHRANE-2026-08-18.md section 1, on Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.4.4: "Decision: REML, everywhere." The estimator this pool used before that date was DerSimonian-Laird inverse-variance on extracted effect estimates; that fit was reproduced first and is quoted under r_output_superseded_2026_08_20, so the movement is attributable rather than asserted.
primary.estimand_established_does_not_cover_the_: READ THIS BESIDE `estimand_established`. That flag records that every contributing trial measures the SAME QUANTITY. It records NOTHING about what that quantity was measured AGAINST -- whether the comparators are of one kind, whether each comparison was randomised, whether it was concurrent. On attr-pn-review the flag is TRUE and correct while the pool combines patisiran against its own saline placebo, vutrisiran against PATISIRAN, and eplontersen against the placebo cohort of a DIFFERENT TRIAL. The two questions were never separated. Named as P48 in PAGE-STANDARD.md v1.21.0 and swept by scripts/audit_mixed_contrast_pools.py.

THE_POOL_IS_REFERRED_2026_08_20.obstacle_means: The registrations state DIFFERENT ENDPOINTS. That is a fact about the trials, not about what this project has got round to reading. Nothing further we do makes these two composites the same composite.
THE_POOL_IS_REFERRED_2026_08_20.primary_defect: THE STROKE COMPONENT IS NOT THE SAME COMPONENT. EMPA-REG's 3-point MACE counts NON-FATAL STROKE OF ANY TYPE; DECLARE's counts ISCHEMIC STROKE ONLY. Haemorrhagic stroke is inside one composite and outside the other. Two different endpoints sharing a name.
THE_POOL_IS_REFERRED_2026_08_20.second_defect: DECLARE registers TWO co-primaries and this review silently used one. The other -- CV death or hospitalisation for heart failure -- is at the same rank and is the endpoint on which DECLARE was positive. An unrecorded selection among co-primaries is an unrecorded analytic decision.
THE_POOL_IS_REFERRED_2026_08_20.AND_THE_OBJECT_ALREADY_SAID_SO: The outcome's own `name` begins 'Multiple trial-declared outcomes:' and then CONCATENATES FOUR DIFFERENT REGISTERED TITLES separated by pipes. `estimand_established` is FALSE. `estimand_id_means` says 'not recorded on the page this object was extracted from'. THREE FIELDS, ALL HONEST, ALL SAYING THE SAME THING -- AND THE POOL PUBLISHED ANYWAY. The defect was never that the object hid this; it is that a published estimate did not have to answer to it.
THE_POOL_IS_REFERRED_2026_08_20.what_would_make_a_pool_defensible: Either restrict to a component set both trials share -- CV death and non-fatal MI, dropping stroke, which is a different and smaller question -- or pool DECLARE's second co-primary against a matching endpoint elsewhere. Both are decisions, not relabellings, and neither is made here.
THE_POOL_IS_REFERRED_2026_08_20.not_withdrawn_because: Withdrawing a published estimate is a published-number decision and belongs to Mahmood. The estimate is unchanged; the finding is complete and stated.

POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.a_a_published_synthesis_carried_more_tri: A PUBLISHED SYNTHESIS OF THIS QUESTION INCLUDED 3 TRIALS WHERE THIS POOL CARRIES 2. Source: Kluger et al., Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2018, PMID 31032602, 'Cardiorenal Outcomes in the CANVAS, DECLARE-TIMI 58, and EMPA-REG OUTCOME Trials'.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.b_whether_the_extra_trials_can_be_named: THE THIRD TRIAL IS NAMED: the CANVAS Program. It is in the title of the review and is not carried by this object. THIS IS THE ONLY TOPIC IN THE CORPUS WHERE A TRIAL WE DO NOT POOL CAN BE NAMED.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.c_what_this_means_for_the_estimate_above: The estimate above is computed from the trials this object carries and is not withdrawn or altered by this note. What a reader is owed is the SCOPE: a larger evidence base on this question exists in the literature, and whether this review's search should be widened is a decision that has not been made.

manuscript.introduction:
This review asks: Multiple trial-declared outcomes: Time to the First Occurrence of Any of the Following Adjudicated Components of the Primary Composite Endpoint (3-point M | Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE) Composite of Cardiovascular (CV) Death, Non-Fatal Myocardial Infarction (MI), | Subjects Included in the Composite Endpoint of CV Death, MI or Ischemic Stroke | Time to First Occurrence of MACE (Composite Endpoint of Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events [Cardiovascular Death, Non-f.

It pools 2 randomised trials, against not recorded on the page this object was extracted from.

The outcome pooled is Multiple trial-declared outcomes: Time to the First Occurrence of Any of the Following Adjudicated Components of the Primary Composite Endpoint (3-point M | Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE) Composite of Cardiovascular (CV) Death, Non-Fatal Myocardial Infarction (MI), | Subjects Included in the Composite Endpoint of CV Death, MI or Ischemic Stroke | Time to First Occurrence of MACE (Composite Endpoint of Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events [Cardiovascular Death, Non-f.

Everything in this paragraph is derived from stored fields and none of it is authored. The interpretive sentences that follow are marked as drafts and are the author's to replace.

absent_from_source.protocol: No protocol or registration record was recoverable from the page.
absent_from_source.search: No search strategy was recoverable from the page.
absent_from_source.screening: No screening log was recoverable from the page.
absent_from_source.rob2: No risk-of-bias assessment was recoverable from the page.
absent_from_source.grade: No certainty rating was recoverable from the page.
absent_from_source.sources: No source registry was recoverable from the page, so no value on this page carries a resolvable link or a quoted source sentence.
absent_from_source.manuscript: No manuscript exists for this review.

display_change_announced.what_changed: `heterogeneity.i2` and `heterogeneity.tau2` are field names that each map to more than one standard definition. Every number is unchanged; each now carries the definition it holds. tau2's definition was already recoverable from the declared `estimator` beside it and is copied, never inferred. i2's was not recoverable and is DECIDED BY RECOMPUTING BOTH FORMS from this object's own per-trial inputs, with the evidence recorded.
display_change_announced.why: A reader recomputing Higgins I-squared from the Q printed beside it would have concluded the object was wrong -- and would have been behaving exactly as we want readers to behave. An ambiguous label on an unambiguous number is a defect specifically against the only reader we claim to serve.

display_change_announced.change: estimator changed to REML -- LABEL ONLY, no value moved
display_change_announced.what_changed: This pool was fitted with DerSimonian-Laird inverse-variance on extracted effect estimates. It is refitted with REML under DECISIONS-COCHRANE-2026-08-18.md section 1, on Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.4.4: "Decision: REML, everywhere." The old fit was reproduced against the stored value FIRST (REPRODUCED) and only then replaced. Stored values are also rounded at storage -- effects to 4 decimals, tau-squared and Q to 6, I-squared to 4 -- because several of these pools carried sixteen significant figures on a two- or three-study pool.
display_change_announced.why: The corpus held two estimator conventions at once: 23 pools REML, 9 DerSimonian-Laird, 1 Paule-Mandel. published_comparison.THE_FINDING_OF_THIS_COMPARISON_2026_08_2: A PUBLISHED SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF THESE EXACT TRIALS LOOKED AT THEM AND DID NOT POOL THEM. Kluger et al. 2018 reported the three CVOTs side by side and concluded that matching inclusion criteria and endpoints would be needed 'to ensure a truly direct comparison of the drugs'. They name the difference: EMPA-REG OUTCOME required prior confirmed cardiovascular disease and enrolled 99.2% with CVD, against 40.6% in DECLARE-TIMI 58. THIS OBJECT POOLS THOSE TWO POPULATIONS INTO ONE ODDS RATIO OF 0.9074. The comparison therefore does not adjudicate our estimate -- IT QUESTIONS WHETHER THE POOL SHOULD EXIST. Withdrawing or restating it is a content decision and is not made here.
